title: The source of emulation
hookLine: Twelver Shia follow a living senior jurist, a marja', in matters of law
last: THE SCHOOL OF THE SIXTH IMAM.

lines: A LIVING NAME ON THE COVER.
cards: On a shelf in a Shia home there may be a thick paperback of numbered rulings. Prayer. Fasting.
Buying and selling. Travel. What to do if you lose count in the middle of a prayer.
The author's name is on the cover, and he's alive. Next door, the shelf may hold the same kind of book by a different author. Each adult in the family may have chosen their own.
Today, the living person a believer follows, and why that person has to be living.

teach.h: MARJA': A SOURCE TO TURN TO.
teach.b: The word is marja': a reference, a place you turn to. In full, marja' al-taqlid, the source of emulation; taqlid means following someone else's ruling. Ja'fari books of practical rulings open with a choice.
In matters of law, an adult can take one of three roads. Become a mujtahid, a jurist able to derive rulings from the sources.
Act with precaution, doing what satisfies every serious opinion, which takes a good deal of knowledge too. Or follow a mujtahid, the road these books expect someone without that training to take.
The one followed is the marja'.
The books list what he must be: adult, sane, just, a Twelver Shia, and a mujtahid. And they add: as best you can tell, follow the most learned, by asking people of knowledge you trust.
Then the condition in today's line: living. In these books, you may not begin following a scholar who has already died.
The reason Shia jurists give: the law keeps meeting new questions, new medicines, new machines, new kinds of money, and a living jurist can answer them. The door of reasoning stays open.

Whether you may stay with a marja' who died while you followed him, they answer differently, and that's a question for your living marja'. This following has limits. It covers practical law: how to pray, fast, trade.
The books ask each person to reach the foundations of belief for themselves.
Shia jurists explain taqlid with a familiar picture: the one who doesn't know turns to the one who does, the way a patient turns to a doctor.

how: Twelver Shia Muslims choose a living marja' whose practical rulings they follow, consulting his book of rulings, his website or his offices with questions about prayer, fasting, trade and daily life.

o: a shrine city where Shia scholars train for many years
the living senior jurist whose rulings a believer follows
a book of numbered rulings kept on a family shelf

games.q: the source of emulation — tap the pairs.

s: in the Ja'fari books, you may begin following a scholar who has died
you begin with a living marja'. staying with one who died is answered differently, and you ask a living marja'.
taqlid covers practical law, like prayer and trade
the books ask each person to reach the foundations of belief for themselves.
following a marja' is the only road the books allow
an adult may become a mujtahid, or act with precaution, or follow one.

games.q: you're a young Shia adult choosing whose rulings to follow. your grandfather followed a great marja' who has since died. what do the books of rulings tell you?
o: begin following the late marja', as your grandfather did.
choose a living marja', the most learned you can identify.
work out every ruling yourself, with no training.
games.why: a living marja', the most learned you can identify by asking trusted people. the law meets new questions, and a living jurist can answer them.

practice: Say the three roads slowly: derive it, be cautious, or follow someone who can.
Then think of one person you lean on who knows more than you, a doctor, a mechanic, an aunt who knows the family recipes, and ask how you chose them and what would make you stop trusting them.
Hold them in mind for a few breaths with some gratitude, and if you pray, you can ask for good guides.

wordCard.voice: Marja'. A source to turn to: in Twelver Shia law, the living senior jurist whose practical rulings a believer follows. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a reference, a place one returns to; marja' al-taqlid, the source of emulation.

carryVoice: Your line: follow the living scholar. New questions keep coming, and a living jurist can answer them. Go gently.

sources.ref: Risalah 'amaliyyah (books of practical rulings by Twelver maraji'), opening rulings on taqlid, ihtiyat and ijtihad
